result:
I've made changes for all six reports and the TypeScript compile is clean. I didn't run the test suite or try any of the scenarios by hand, so none of the six fixes has been exercised.

- **Keys and addresses.** Project addresses and keys are now checked against every project in the workspace, archived ones included. A taken key gets a number appended and is trimmed so it stays within four characters ("WV" becomes "WV2"). This is in `project-repository.ts`, using a new `uniqueProjectKey` in `lib/slug.ts`.
- **Plan slots.** Only live projects count against the plan limit. Restoring is refused when the plan has no room, before anything is restored or announced. The projects meter now goes up by one on restore, through a new `project.restored` listener in `usage-service.ts`.
- **Restoring.** Restoring a project that isn't archived is refused and announces nothing.
- **Status.** The saved status is now written by `updateProject`; before, the repository ignored it. In `project-service.ts`, completing a project with open issues is refused, and archived and done/canceled issues don't count as open. Completing an already-completed project is a no-op, and pausing and reactivating are always allowed. In `issue-service.ts`, creating an issue in a paused or completed project is refused.

I didn't change the status permission, because `updateProject` already requires `project:update`, which is the right needed to edit the project.
